parts.text:
Check the empty-and-objects case: `check('', ['1.2a1'], ['1.2a1'])` — empty spec, prereleases None. New filter: specs empty, so prereleases None; item 1.2a1 is prerelease, contained (empty specs contains → True with prereleases=True in the all check). prereleases is None, so appended to pending, found_final=False → yield 1.2a1. OK.

`check('', ['1.2a1'], [], call=False)`: prereleases False; item prerelease, prereleases not True → skipped. OK.

`check('', ['1.2a1','1.1'], ['1.1'])`: 1.2a1 pending, 1.1 not prerelease → found_final True, yield 1.1, pending not yielded. OK.

`check('>=1,<2', ['1.5a1','1.4.post1'], ['1.4.post1'])` fine.

`'>1.0,<2', ['1.0.post1','1.1a1']` → ['1.1a1']: 1.0.post1 not prerelease but not in range (>1.0 excludes? 1.0.post1 >1.0 — actually Version('1.0.post1') > Version('1.0'), so it IS >1.0. Post release: 1.0.post1 > 1.0 yes. Not prerelease. So found_final=True, yield 1.0.post1. But expected only ['1.1a1']!

Check upstream behavior: packaging's Specifier '>1.0' — does 1.0.post1 satisfy >1.0? Actually packaging specifiers exclude post-releases for >V... For Specifier without wildcard: for operator '>' the spec says "excluded post releases of the specified version" — upstream code: if the operator is > or >=, the item's base_version compared... Actually in packaging Specifier._compare_greater_than: it checks if the item is a post-release of the specified version and returns False. Specifically: "if item is a post release of the specified version, return False" for > and >=. Yes, upstream: `if Version(prospective.base_version) == Version(spec.base_version): return False` for > operator. So 1.0.post1 excluded by '>1.0'. Good, expected ['1.1a1'].

But the requirement note "version ordering alone is not specifier membership" — the filter uses s.contains(parsed, prereleases=True), which handles that. OK.

Bounds: '>=1.5a1,<2', ['1.5a1','1.6'] → both. prereleases: any spec prereleases → True. 1.5a1: contains with prereleases=True → yes, prereleases is True → yield. OK.

'>=1,<2,!=1.5a1', ['1.5a1','1.6rc1','3'] → ['1.6rc1']: prereleases any→True, 1.6rc1 passes !=, yield. 3 excluded. OK.

Matching finals: '>=1,<2', ['1.5a1','1.4','2.1','1.6rc1','1.4'] → ['1.4','1.4']. prereleases: any spec prereleases? '>=1' prereleases False; '<2' False; no. prereleases None. 1.5a1 pending; 1.4 found_final yield; 1.6rc1 pending. Result ['1.4','1.4'] identity: yields original items. But duplicates: '1.4' appears twice, both yielded with identity. OK.

Fallback: '>=1,<2', ['0.9','1.5a1','2.1'] → ['1.5a1']. prereleases None. 1.5a1 pending; no finals → yield. OK.

Explicit cases: constructor=True: prereleases True → yield prerelease and final, found_final True. OK. constructor=False, call=True: prereleases True → fine.

Duplicate-final-identity: consumed checked fully — new filter consumes entire iterable. seen == original requires consuming all. Yes.

Individual Specifier.filter unchanged (old code retained at 23070). Contains preserved.

Hmm, but individual-filter: `Specifier('>=1').filter(iter(values))` uses old Specifier.filter; values include string '2.0'; result[1] is values[2]. Old code yields version (original). contains dispatch ok. Wait old Specifier.filter kw prereleases True inside contains — '>=1' prereleases for spec: Specifier('>=1').prereleases is False, but kw True → contains True. '0.9' excluded, result len 2. OK.

Empty spec and prereleases detection: `any(s.prereleases for s in self._specs)` — empty specs → False, prereleases stays None. Fine.

Anything wrong? What about item identity in duplicate-final case with left, right equal versions — filter yields parsed? No, yields item. OK.

What about `check('>=1,<2', ['1.5a1','1.4.post1'], ['1.4.post1'])` — 1.4.post1 not prerelease, yield, found_final True. 1.5a1 pending not yielded. Good.

One concern: in `selected()`, items that fail containment skip; fine. Item is str like '2.0'? Grader passes strings only as values list for check; str comparisons — result str(v) fine.

Dev releases: `parsed.is_prerelease` includes dev releases; upstream filter also treats dev as prerelease. Fine.

contains-policy unchanged: contains checks prereleases property. OK.

I don't find a wrong repair. Maybe subtle: new filter ignores `self._specs` empty but prereleases True in set? Not tested.

One possible: in the new filter, when prereleases is None and any spec has prereleases=True, prereleases=True — then ALL prereleases in range yielded even without finals. e.g. bounds-and-exclusions case '>=1.5a1,<2' expects both yielded. Matches upstream? Upstream: kw prereleases True when self.prereleases None → yields everything in-range regardless of finals. Requirement says "prerelease bounds" — allowed. Matches grader anyway.

Submit empty findings.

I reviewed the new SpecifierSet.filter implementation against every grader case: fallback, matching-finals, explicit policies, bounds/exclusions (including the `>1.0` post-release exclusion, which Specifier.contains handles via base_version comparison), empty-set/Version-object/one-shot behavior, contains policy, individual Specifier.filter (untouched upstream code), and duplicate identity with full-consumption assertions. I traced the `selected()` logic (pending prereleases, found_final suppression, identity of yielded items, single pass) and the unchanged `contains` dispatch for each case; all expected outputs and identity/consumption assertions hold. I found no wrong repair or contradictory assertion.
